doc.title: Rick Montalbano interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, August 12, 2011

chapter: Sixties rock and listening to Miles
title: Playing sixties rock and buying a Hammond organ
summary: He played current rock in 1967-68 bands, including Beatles, Stones and Steppenwolf songs, and bought a Hammond organ at 17 or 18 with gig money.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: What would have been the repertoire for the rock stuff you were doing? This was from the sixties?

Yeah, yeah. The Beatles. One group was like, in those days, it was like ’67, ’68, we called it hard rock. Today I don’t know if you would call it heavy metal or, I don’t know. But there was a lot of English groups, The Easy Beats, and of course the Rolling Stones and the Beatles stuff and loud rock & roll. Yeah. Not fifties rock & roll. Definitely 60’s rock & roll.
In other words, you guys were playing current material.
Yeah, we were playing the music of the day. Steppenwolf and I had a Hammond organ by that point.
That must have been a big investment.

Yeah. Yeah. I bought that when I was, I don’t know, 17, 18 years old. It comes from all those years, honestly, of just making money. I always had a pocketful of money from playing gigs. I wish I did today.
